title: State Auditor reports not already listed
question: Beyond the reports already listed under official documents, has the State Auditor said anything else about San Francisco or a program it runs?
finding: Nothing adverse. The 16 reports that examine San Francisco are in the official-documents screen; the remaining 4 that mention the city often are 3 audits of the State Bar, a State body whose head office was in San Francisco, and 1 audit of Anaheim's stadium lease, which uses the Port of San Francisco's lease with the Giants as the better example.
how: The State Auditor's catalog for 2018 to 2026 was screened for reports that name a San Francisco body or mention San Francisco ten times or more. Those already listed in this project's record screen were set aside; for each of the rest, one sentence that mentions San Francisco was taken from the report text, cut to 25 words.
limits: The screening rule is mechanical: a report can mention San Francisco many times only because a State body has an office or a building there. No State Auditor report in these years has the City and County of San Francisco as its main subject. Nine reports in the catalog are image-only files with no readable text and could not be searched.
